relevance_note: Family case report of Tangier disease with individual-level data for ABCA1 carriers: "This mutation was found in homozygosity in DC e RC and in heterozygosity in CC".
method_note: Hand-built by a short Python script from my reading; every span checked verbatim by script. Persons: proband AC, sisters DC and CC, brother RC (initials are the paper's labels), and the two heterozygous sons of DC and AC. 'the two sons of DC and AC' does not say which son belongs to whom (or whether both belong to one), so they are labelled 'son of DC and AC' and 'son of DC and AC 2'; inheritance recorded as 'inherited maternal' because both possible mothers (DC, AC) are stated homozygous (Table 2 Genotype row; text). Out of scope (not tested, no features): parents (first-degree cousins), one brother born dead, one brother who died 2 days after birth of pneumonia. Proband polymorphisms called benign by in silico analysis were not described and get no rows. Table 2 has patients as columns (DC, AC, CC, RC); Table 1 (electrophysiology, columns DC R/L, CC R/L, AC R/L, RC R/L) was not transcribed nerve by nerve; neuropathy features come from the text. 'Other blood tests were normal' is unspecific (no person named, no test named) and excludes nothing. Abdomen US 'without visceromegaly' (performed to seek visceromegaly) taken to exclude splenomegaly and hepatomegaly for AC. Aortic intimal-medial thickening with atheroma recorded as non-coronary atherosclerotic disease; MI treated with bypass recorded as coronary artery disease. Possible tension: Discussion says the picture 'but not of kidney function impairment ... nor cardiomyopathy' should point to ABCA1-associated TD, while AC's echocardiogram showed 'initial signs of dilated cardiomyopathy'; the Discussion sentence names no person, so no excluded rows were emitted. 'DC presents clinical findings similar to AC' was not used to copy features. CC's HDL (44, reference >45) is described as 'not presenting very low HDL-C', so low HDL is not reported for CC. Disease label recorded only for AC ('suggested diagnosis of TD'); DC and RC are homozygous but the paper gives no individual diagnosis label. Vital status left not reported (ages given in present tense only).
